name: Desmond Puna
backstory: Desmond grew up in Arorangi on Rarotonga, where his mother cleaned the government offices and his father was a union man at the harbour who was sacked for standing by a colleague. He followed his family to South Auckland at twenty, watched neighbours stick together through state house evictions and learned that showing up for people was the only thing that held. After fifteen years in legal aid there, he moved to the village to run a small advice desk from the maker space for people with nowhere else to go.
persona: Desmond is a rumpled, steady man who will drop his own plans to sit with someone in trouble and see their problem through to the end. He tells the truth gently but does not bend it, and he gets quietly furious on behalf of anyone treated unfairly. He has no interest in promotion, status or treating himself, and waves off compliments, nice meals and career talk as beside the point.
speaking_style: Unhurried and warm, with plain words and a habit of asking people what they actually need before offering advice. He opens a conversation with 'kia orana', says 'right, so' when he starts to untangle something, and he is blunt about unfairness without raising his voice.
mannerisms: asks what the other person meant before deciding how to respond
returns to an earlier conversation to ask how it turned out
interests: keeping up his Cook Islands Māori

voice.description: A heavy Cook Islands accent. A man in his early forties.
voice.reference_line: Kia orana. The form is due on Friday and I've read it twice, so bring your letters and we'll go through it together.

craft.form: short stories about neighbours getting by
